scope: Program-level compliance requirements that the platform must satisfy, taken only from the Associates Operating Agreement, the Program Policies, the Standard Commission Income Statement and FTC materials. Each requirement carries a verbatim or near-verbatim quote and a source id. Status values: 'implemented' = the rule is met on the current build; 'gated' = the rule is deliberately not met until an account-only or evidence-only step that this repository cannot perform on its own is completed, and the blocker is named in status_note.

requirements.requirement: The site must clearly and prominently state the Associate identification statement.
requirements.quote: “You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: ‘As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.’”
requirements.how_implemented: The exact sentence appears below the masthead, before main, and repeats in the footer of every canonical generated page.

implementation_history.how_implemented: The statement appears in the persistent header disclosure bar and in the footer of every page generated by build.py.

requirements.topic: Link-level disclosure must be clear and conspicuous
requirements.requirement: Beyond the site-wide statement, each affiliate link needs a clear, nearby, FTC-compliant disclosure.
requirements.quote: “To comply with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) regulations, your link-level disclosure must be: 1. Clear. A clear disclosure could be as simple as ‘(paid link)’, ‘#ad’, or ‘#CommissionsEarned’. 2. Conspicuous. It should be placed near any affiliate link or product review in a location that customers will notice easily. They shouldn't have to hunt for it.”
requirements.how_implemented: Main product CTAs identify Amazon and repeat the affiliate relationship and unconfirmed intended-listing/attribution boundary beside the action. Every real Amazon product anchor is qualified sponsored, including source citations.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Every outbound Amazon button carries a visible “Paid link” tag, and a disclosure note sits directly beneath each CTA.

requirements.requirement: Disclosures must be hard to miss, in the same medium as the endorsement, and must not be buried or mixed into hashtags.
requirements.quote: “Make sure people will see and understand the disclosure. Place it so it's hard to miss. The disclosure should be placed with the endorsement message itself. Disclosures are likely to be missed if they appear only on an ABOUT ME or profile page, at the end of posts or videos, or anywhere that requires a person to click MORE. Don't mix your disclosure into a group of hashtags or links.”
requirements.how_implemented: Disclosure bar is above the fold on every page; per-link badges; no disclosure-only-in-footer pattern.

requirements.requirement: A financial relationship with the seller must be disclosed.
requirements.quote: When there exists a connection between the endorser and the seller of the advertised product that might materially affect the weight or credibility of the endorsement, and that connection is not reasonably expected by the audience, such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
requirements.how_implemented: The potential financial relationship is disclosed in the strip, beside main product CTAs and in the footer. No credited click, order or earnings report is claimed.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Commission-earning relationship disclosed in the header, on each CTA and on the compliance page.

requirements.requirement: Prices and availability may only be displayed if Amazon serves them or they are obtained through Creators API/PA API.
requirements.quote: “Because prices for and availability of Products that you have listed on your Site may change, your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements…”
requirements.how_implemented: No Amazon price or availability is shown anywhere. Manufacturer list prices are shown separately and explicitly labelled as brand-site prices with their own source link.

requirements.requirement: Amazon reviews/star ratings may only be displayed when obtained through Creators API or PA API.
requirements.quote: “You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API and you comply with the requirements for Creators API and PA API described in the License.”
requirements.clause: Program Policies — Participation Requirements §6(t) ("Content on your Site"; live page read 2026-11-14 — see flag F27)
requirements.how_implemented: No authorised Amazon review/rating integration is configured. Dated brand-widget snapshots are separately labelled in the evidence data, not used as Amazon ratings, test results or product rankings.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Amazon stars/review counts blank and flagged. Brand-hosted ratings are shown only in a clearly separate column, attributed to the brand's own site.

requirements.topic: No price tracking or price alerts
requirements.requirement: Sites must not offer price tracking or price alerting unless Amazon agrees otherwise.
requirements.quote: “Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality.”
requirements.clause: Program Policies — Participation Requirements §6(y) ("Content on your Site"; live page read 2026-11-14 — see flag F27)
requirements.how_implemented: No price-history, alert, deal-timer or lowest-ever component ships. No revenue scenario or conversion score is used to justify design. Any future authorised exception requires a separate current permission/terms review.

implementation_history.how_implemented: The platform blueprint explicitly rules out price-history charts and alerts; ‘pricing analysis’ is limited to brand-published list prices and unit economics computed from them.

requirements.requirement: No bidding on Amazon or Kindle trademarks, or any Amazon Mark, in paid search.
requirements.quote: “…any Product purchased by a customer who is referred to an Amazon Site through any advertisement that you purchased, including through participation in bidding or auctions on keywords, search terms, or other identifiers that include the word ‘amazon’, or ‘kindle’, or any other Amazon Mark…” (disqualified purchases)
requirements.how_implemented: The paid-search restriction is recorded in the blueprint. No paid campaign, live bidding workflow or enforced account negative-keyword configuration is deployed or claimed.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Guardrail G3 in the platform blueprint: a negative-keyword list containing Amazon Marks is enforced in the paid-acquisition workflow.

requirements.topic: No API content aggregation, analysis or model training
requirements.requirement: Creators API / PA API / Data Feeds content may not be aggregated, analysed, repurposed, or used to train or fine-tune ML models.
requirements.quote: “You will not, without our express prior written approval, access or use Creators API, PA API or Data Feeds for the purpose of aggregating, analyzing, extracting, or repurposing any Product Advertising Content or in connection with any software or other application intended for use by persons or entities that offer products on an Amazon Site, or in the direct training or fine-tuning of a machine learning and/or foundational model.”
requirements.how_implemented: No authorised API/content-analysis feed or running trend scorer is configured. Future access and permitted-use review are separate gates; the static builder does not grant rights to analyse or train on Program Content.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Architectural constraint: any AI research/trend scoring runs only on the operator's own first-party data (clicks, conversions, revenue) and public manufacturer data. Program Content is display-only, never a training or analytics input.

requirements.requirement: Sites must carry robust original content — roughly 10+ posts, recent, publicly available.
requirements.quote: “All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) – a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts. They must be publicly available…” and “Content on your website must be recent (generally within the last 60 days). You must own your website.”
requirements.how_implemented: This build ships analysis, comparison and buying-guide pages written for this dataset, plus the platform blueprint — not a thin link list.

requirements.requirement: Applications are reviewed after three qualifying sales within the first 180 days; personal orders do not count.
requirements.quote: “After you sign up, our Associates team will check your application once you’ve driven qualified sales (we require at least three within the first 180 days). Please note that personal orders do not qualify.”
requirements.how_implemented: Public criteria remain a dated policy record, not a claim about this account’s approval, qualifying sales or review-window start. PUB-1 did not freshly re-read the application criteria page or access the account.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Launch sequencing in the blueprint: publish the buying guide + three product pages first, then apply, so the 180-day clock starts with live traffic.

requirements.topic: No incentive for using links; no self-purchase
requirements.requirement: No rewards/loyalty schemes driving clicks; no buying through your own links or asking friends/family to.
requirements.quote: “You will not offer any person or entity any consideration, reward, or incentive (including any money, rebate, discount, points, donation to charity or other organization, or other benefit) for using Special Links…” / “You will not directly or indirectly purchase any Product(s)… through Special Links…”
requirements.clause: Participation Requirements §6(g) and §6(u) ("Content on your Site"; live page read 2026-11-14 — see flag F27)
requirements.how_implemented: No incentives, no contests, no employee purchase flows. Guardrail G4.

requirements.topic: No framing, no cloaking, no redirecting links
requirements.requirement: Amazon pages may not be framed; Special Links may not be cloaked; redirecting links that skip user action are prohibited.
requirements.quote: “You will not frame an Amazon Site, or any part of it, within your Site…” / “You will not cloak, hide, spoof, or otherwise obscure the URL of your Site containing Special Links (including by use of Redirecting Links)…”
requirements.clause: Participation Requirements §6(n) and §6(v) ("Content on your Site"; live page read 2026-11-14 — see flag F27)
requirements.how_implemented: No iframes. Outbound links point straight at the Amazon URL; no interstitial or meta-refresh forwarding is generated by the site.

requirements.requirement: Reporting IDs are permitted, but they may not be tied to an individual end user.
requirements.quote: “…we may issue you additional ‘sub-tag’ Associate IDs that permit you to monitor and optimize the performance of your Special Links… Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users’ behavior).”
requirements.how_implemented: shopnow047c-20 is selected but unvalidated and unapplied. No channel/page IDs have been created or assigned by this build. Any later approved ID plan must not identify individual visitors.

implementation_history.how_implemented: Sub-tags are assigned per channel/page, never per visitor. Documented as guardrail G5.

requirements.requirement: Amazon Marks may be used only to advertise availability of products on an Amazon Site, alongside a corresponding Special Link, unaltered, and never in offline material.
requirements.quote: “YOU ARE ALLOWED TO USE THE AMAZON MARKS ONLY BY DISPLAY ON YOUR SITE WITH THE PURPOSE OF ADVERTISING AVAILABILITY OF PRODUCTS ON AN AMAZON SITE, WITH A CORRESPONDING SPECIAL LINK TO THAT SITE.”
requirements.how_implemented: No Amazon logo is copied into the canonical publication. Plain-text Amazon labels make outbound destinations clear; this is not evidence that an enrolled Special Link or account has been validated.

implementation_history.how_implemented: No Amazon logo is used in this build; Amazon is referred to in plain text next to real Special Links only.

requirements.requirement: No inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or misleading product/policy/price claims; no claiming an experience you have not had.
requirements.quote: “You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product, an Amazon Site, or any of our policies, promotions, or prices.” / FTC: “You can't talk about your experience with a product you haven't tried.”
requirements.how_implemented: AI-assisted document research and no hands-on testing are disclosed. Revised guide claims cite named official sections; uncertain values and conflicts remain explicit. Link coverage alone is not proof that arbitrary prose is true.

implementation_history.how_implemented: No hands-on testing claims are made anywhere. Copy is explicitly framed as documentation-based analysis, and every factual line links to the manufacturer page or manual.

requirements.topic: Agents must identify themselves, must not obfuscate, must not defeat bot checks
requirements.requirement: If software or a service takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action on the Program Content, it is an “Agent”: it must identify itself in every HTTP/HTTPS request, must not conceal that it is an agent, must not complete or circumvent CAPTCHAs, and must answer truthfully when asked whether the interactions are human.
requirements.quote: “The terms in this section (“Agent Terms”) apply if you use, allow, enable, or cause the deployment of an Agent to access, use, or interact with the Program Content. For the purposes of these Agent Terms, “Agent” means any software or service that takes autonomous or semi-autonomous action on behalf of, or at the instruction of, any person or entity.” … “In all HTTP/HTTPS requests, identify that the request is from an Agent and disclose the name of the Agent by including the following in the request’s user agent string: “Agent/[agent name]” (e.g., Agent/AmazonAgent)” … “Not conceal or obfuscate that any access, use, or interactions are from an Agent, such as by (a) mimicking the speed or pattern of human keystrokes, page navigation, or other interactions or (b) completing or circumventing CAPTCHAs or other measures intended to distinguish computers from humans. Respond truthfully to any question or prompt seeking to determine if interactions are coming from a human or a computer.”
requirements.clause: Program Policies — Associates Program IP License §4 (Agents). Read live 2026-11-16 by arena/9fccce0c-zone1; the whole of §4 was not read end to end in that pass (flag F62).
requirements.how_implemented: No unattended network research agent is deployed by this static build. The Agent Terms and identity/access requirements are recorded as future research gates. This is not a legal finding that no Agent Term can apply to an external tool or to every future use.

implementation_history.how_implemented: The build's fetch layer is not an autonomous agent and this site consumes no Program Content at all, so no Agent Term is triggered by anything the site publishes today. The platform blueprint that proposes automated research carries the rule as guardrail G11, and the research-agent design decision is queued as SG-22 rather than decided here.

requirements.topic: No Special Links or Program Content used to develop machine-learning models without approval
requirements.requirement: An Associate may not use Special Links or Program Content — or allow a third party to do so — to develop machine-learning models or related technology, without Amazon's express prior written approval.
requirements.quote: “You will not, without express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology.”
requirements.clause: Program Policies — Participation Requirements §5 (Distribution of Special Links Through Software and Devices). Read live 2026-11-16 by arena/9fccce0c-zone1.
requirements.how_implemented: This repository implements no model-training/fine-tuning pipeline. Future Special Link or Program Content use requires current permission/terms review; no API credentials, written approval or legal entitlement are invented.

implementation_history.how_implemented: No model in this project is trained on Program Content and none is planned to be. The site's copy is generated by a template, not by a model fitted on Amazon data; the platform blueprint keeps Program Content display-only (guardrail G6).

requirements.topic: The Associates tag must be a URL parameter on every Special Link
requirements.requirement: A tracked outbound link is not merely a product URL. Amazon requires the Associates ID ("tag") to appear as a parameter in the URL of each link placed on the site, requires Special Links to be accessed directly from the site, forbids encouraging visitors to bookmark them, and makes the link the unit at which a Qualifying Purchase is created: a purchase can only be credited if it follows a click through a Special Link.
requirements.quote: “All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site. For example, you must include your Associates ID or ‘tag’ (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site.” — and “We will pay Standard Commission Income … in connection with ‘Qualifying Purchases’, which … occur when: (a) a customer clicks through a Special Link on your Site to an Amazon Site”.
requirements.clause: Program Policies — Participation Requirements §2(b); Commission Income Statement §1
requirements.how_implemented: NOT SATISFIED ON THE PUBLISHED BUILD, BY DESIGN. data/config.json keeps associate_tag empty, so every outbound product anchor the generator emits is an untagged product URL: it can send a reader to the right listing but cannot create an attributed Qualifying Purchase. That is the correct state until the account-holder checks in F76 pass, because the repository must not invent a tag or claim attribution it has not observed. The consequence is stated plainly rather than buried: while the tag is blank the affiliate revenue path is not operating, regardless of how much traffic the pages earn. Enabling it is a configuration change, not a rewrite — the generator already routes every product anchor through one builder and qualifies every one sponsored. Gates: build.py refuses to write a tag that has not been confirmed in Associates Central or whose per-product enrolled test is unrecorded; verify.py re-checks that no unverified tag reached the output.
requirements.status_note: Deliberately gated, not overlooked. The blocker is an account-only verification step, recorded as F76 (tracking ID) and F77 (intended listing) on the Flagged page, and re-read live on 2026-11-20 against the Program Policies page and the Application Review page (see data/sources.json reverified_2026_11_20_69c1201a). The Application Review page adds a consequence worth stating plainly: it lists rejection for not using special 'tagged' links as a known outcome and says an application cannot be reassessed once rejected, so this site should not be submitted as a declared traffic source while its links carry no observable tag.
